subject: Nanotechnology
title: Asymmetric Supercapacitors
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Asymmetric Supercapacitors.

hook.text: Use a different material for each electrode and the voltage window doubles — asymmetric supercapacitors store more.

buildup.text: One electrode uses carbon for capacitive storage; the other uses a metal oxide for faradaic pseudo-capacitance.

discovery.text: The wider voltage window increases energy density by the square of voltage — a huge gain from one change.

twist.text: Balancing charge between two different electrodes is tricky — mass ratio and kinetics must match precisely.

climax.text: Nano-MnO₂ paired with activated carbon reaches energy densities rivaling some batteries — with capacitor-speed charge.

punchline.text: Two different nano electrodes double the voltage and quadruple the energy.

quiz.question: Why do asymmetric supercapacitors have higher energy density?
options: Different electrode materials widen the voltage window, and energy scales with voltage squared
